NKJV.1: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Depart and go up from here, you and the people whom you have brought out of the land of Egypt, to the land of which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘To your descendants I will give it.’
NKJV.2: And I will send My Angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanite and the Amorite and the Hittite and the Perizzite and the Hivite and the Jebusite.
NKJV.3: Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey; for I will not go up in your midst, lest I consume you on the way, for you are a stiff-necked people.”
NKJV.4: And when the people heard this bad news, they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.
NKJV.5: For the LORD had said to Moses, “Say to the children of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. I could come up into your midst in one moment and consume you. Now therefore, take off your ornaments, that I may know what to do to you.’ ”
NKJV.6: So the children of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments by Mount Horeb.
NKJV.7: Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, far from the camp, and called it the tabernacle of meeting. And it came to pass that everyone who sought the LORD went out to the tabernacle of meeting which was outside the camp.
NKJV.8: So it was, whenever Moses went out to the tabernacle, that all the people rose, and each man stood at his tent door and watched Moses until he had gone into the tabernacle.
NKJV.9: And it came to pass, when Moses entered the tabernacle, that the pillar of cloud descended and stood at the door of the tabernacle, and the LORD talked with Moses.
NKJV.10: All the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the tabernacle door, and all the people rose and worshiped, each man in his tent door.
NKJV.11: So the LORD spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. And he would return to the camp, but his servant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, did not depart from the tabernacle.
NKJV.12: Then Moses said to the LORD, “See, You say to me, ‘Bring up this people.’ But You have not let me know whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found grace in My sight.’
NKJV.13: Now therefore, I pray, if I have found grace in Your sight, show me now Your way, that I may know You and that I may find grace in Your sight. And consider that this nation is Your people.”
NKJV.14: And He said, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
NKJV.15: Then he said to Him, “If Your Presence does not go with us, do not bring us up from here.
NKJV.16: For how then will it be known that Your people and I have found grace in Your sight, except You go with us? So we shall be separate, Your people and I, from all the people who are upon the face of the earth.”
NKJV.17: So the LORD said to Moses, “I will also do this thing that you have spoken; for you have found grace in My sight, and I know you by name.”
NKJV.18: And he said, “Please, show me Your glory.”
NKJV.19: Then He said, “I will make all My goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the name of the LORD before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.”
NKJV.20: But He said, “You cannot see My face; for no man shall see Me, and live.”
NKJV.21: And the LORD said, “Here is a place by Me, and you shall stand on the rock.
NKJV.22: So it shall be, while My glory passes by, that I will put you in the cleft of the rock, and will cover you with My hand while I pass by.
NKJV.23: Then I will take away My hand, and you shall see My back; but My face shall not be seen.”

ESV.1: The LORD said to Moses, “Depart; go up from here, you and the people whom you have brought up out of the land of Egypt, to the land of which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, ‘To your offspring I will give it.’
ESV.2: I will send an angel before you, and I will drive out the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
ESV.3: Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey; but I will not go up among you, lest I consume you on the way, for you are a stiff-necked people.”
ESV.4: When the people heard this disastrous word, they mourned, and no one put on his ornaments.
ESV.5: For the LORD had said to Moses, “Say to the people of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people; if for a single moment I should go up among you, I would consume you. So now take off your ornaments, that I may know what to do with you.’”
ESV.6: Therefore the people of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments, from Mount Horeb onward.
ESV.7: Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, far off from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. And everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting, which was outside the camp.
ESV.8: Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise up, and each would stand at his tent door, and watch Moses until he had gone into the tent.
ESV.9: When Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and the LORD  would speak with Moses.
ESV.10: And when all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, all the people would rise up and worship, each at his tent door.
ESV.11: Thus the LORD used to speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. When Moses turned again into the camp, his assistant Joshua the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the tent.
ESV.12: Moses said to the LORD, “See, you say to me, ‘Bring up this people,’ but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.’
ESV.13: Now therefore, if I have found favor in your sight, please show me now your ways, that I may know you in order to find favor in your sight. Consider too that this nation is your people.”
ESV.14: And he said, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
ESV.15: And he said to him, “If your presence will not go with me, do not bring us up from here.
ESV.16: For how shall it be known that I have found favor in your sight, I and your people? Is it not in your going with us, so that we are distinct, I and your people, from every other people on the face of the earth?”
ESV.17: And the LORD said to Moses, “This very thing that you have spoken I will do, for you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name.”
ESV.18: Moses said, “Please show me your glory.”
ESV.19: And he said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you and will proclaim before you my name ‘The LORD.’ And I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.
ESV.20: But,” he said, “you cannot see my face, for man shall not see me and live.”
ESV.21: And the LORD said, “Behold, there is a place by me where you shall stand on the rock,
ESV.22: and while my glory passes by I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and I will cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
ESV.23: Then I will take away my hand, and you shall see my back, but my face shall not be seen.”

NASB.1: Then the LORD spoke to Moses, 'Depart, go up from here, you and the people whom you have brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land of which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying, 'To your descendants I will give it.'
NASB.2: 'I will send an angel before you and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite and the Jebusite.
NASB.3: '[Go up] to a land flowing with milk and honey; for I will not go up in your midst, because you are an obstinate people, and I might destroy you on the way.'
NASB.4: When the people heard this sad word, they went into mourning, and none of them put on his ornaments.
NASB.5: For the LORD had said to Moses, 'Say to the sons of Israel, 'You are an obstinate people; should I go up in your midst for one moment, I would destroy you. Now therefore, put off your ornaments from you, that I may know what I shall do with you.''
NASB.6: So the sons of Israel stripped themselves of their ornaments, from Mount Horeb [onward].
NASB.7: Now Moses used to take the tent and pitch it outside the camp, a good distance from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting. And everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the tent of meeting which was outside the camp.
NASB.8: And it came about, whenever Moses went out to the tent, that all the people would arise and stand, each at the entrance of his tent, and gaze after Moses until he entered the tent.
NASB.9: Whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent; and the LORD would speak with Moses.
NASB.10: When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, all the people would arise and worship, each at the entrance of his tent.
NASB.11: Thus the LORD used to speak to Moses face to face, just as a man speaks to his friend. When Moses returned to the camp, his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the tent.
NASB.12: Then Moses said to the LORD, 'See, You say to me, 'Bring up this people!' But You Yourself have not let me know whom You will send with me. Moreover, You have said, 'I have known you by name, and you have also found favor in My sight.'
NASB.13: 'Now therefore, I pray You, if I have found favor in Your sight, let me know Your ways that I may know You, so that I may find favor in Your sight. Consider too, that this nation is Your people.'
NASB.14: And He said, 'My presence shall go [with you], and I will give you rest.'
NASB.15: Then he said to Him, 'If Your presence does not go [with us], do not lead us up from here.
NASB.16: 'For how then can it be known that I have found favor in Your sight, I and Your people? Is it not by Your going with us, so that we, I and Your people, may be distinguished from all the [other] people who are upon the face of the earth?'
NASB.17: The LORD said to Moses, 'I will also do this thing of which you have spoken; for you have found favor in My sight and I have known you by name.'
NASB.18: Then Moses said, 'I pray You, show me Your glory!'
NASB.19: And He said, 'I Myself will make all My goodness pass before you, and will proclaim the name of the LORD before you; and I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show compassion on whom I will show compassion.'
NASB.20: But He said, 'You cannot see My face, for no man can see Me and live!'
NASB.21: Then the LORD said, 'Behold, there is a place by Me, and you shall stand [there] on the rock;
NASB.22: and it will come about, while My glory is passing by, that I will put you in the cleft of the rock and cover you with My hand until I have passed by.
NASB.23: 'Then I will take My hand away and you shall see My back, but My face shall not be seen.'

CSB17.1: The LORD spoke to Moses: “Go up from here, you and the people you brought up from the land of Egypt, to the land I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying: I will give it to your offspring. <sup>ⓔ</sup>
CSB17.2: I will send an angel ahead of you and will drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hethites, Perizzites, <sup>[1]</sup> Hivites, and Jebusites. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.3: Go up to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up with you because you are a stiff-necked people; otherwise, I might destroy you on the way.” <sup>ⓖ</sup>
CSB17.4: When the people heard this bad news, they mourned and didn’t put on their jewelry. <sup>ⓗ</sup>
CSB17.5: For the LORD said to Moses: “Tell the Israelites: You are a stiff-necked people. If I went up with you for a single moment, I would destroy you. Now take off your jewelry, and I will decide what to do with you.”
CSB17.6: So the Israelites remained stripped of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.
CSB17.7: Now Moses took a tent and pitched it outside the camp, at a distance from the camp; he called it the tent of meeting. Anyone who wanted to consult the LORD would go to the tent of meeting that was outside the camp. <sup>ⓘ</sup>
CSB17.8: Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would stand up, each one at the door of his tent, and they would watch Moses until he entered the tent.
CSB17.9: When Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and remain at the entrance to the tent, and the LORD would speak with Moses. <sup>ⓙ</sup>
CSB17.10: As all the people saw the pillar of cloud remaining at the entrance to the tent, they would stand up, then bow in worship, each one at the door of his tent.
CSB17.11: The LORD would speak with Moses face to face, just as a man speaks with his friend, then Moses would return to the camp. His assistant, the young man Joshua son of Nun, would not leave the inside of the tent. <sup>ⓚ</sup>
CSB17.12: Moses said to the LORD, “Look, you have told me, ‘Lead this people up,’ but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. You said, ‘I know you by name, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and you have also found favor with me.’
CSB17.13: Now if I have indeed found favor with you, please teach me your ways, <sup>ⓜ</sup> and I will know you, so that I may find favor with you. Now consider that this nation is your people.” <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.14: And he replied, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.” <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.15: “If your presence does not go,” Moses responded to him, “don’t make us go up from here.
CSB17.16: How will it be known that I and your people have found favor with you unless you go with us? I and your people will be distinguished by this from all the other people on the face of the earth.” <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.17: The LORD answered Moses, “I will do this very thing you have asked, for you have found favor with me, and I know you by name.”
CSB17.18: Then Moses said, “Please, let me see your glory.” <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.19: He said, “I will cause all my goodness to pass in front of you, and I will proclaim the name ‘the LORD’ before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.” <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.20: But he added, “You cannot see my face, for humans cannot see <sup>ⓔ</sup> me and live.”
CSB17.21: The LORD said, “Here is a place near me. You are to stand on the rock,
CSB17.22: and when my glory passes by, I will put you in the crevice of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.23: Then I will take my hand away, and you will see my back, but my face will not be seen.”

NLT.1: The LORD said to Moses, “Get going, you and the people you brought up from the land of Egypt. Go up to the land I swore to give to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I told them, ‘I will give this land to your descendants.’
NLT.2: And I will send an angel before you to drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
NLT.3: Go up to this land that flows with milk and honey. But I will not travel among you, for you are a stubborn and rebellious people. If I did, I would surely destroy you along the way.”
NLT.4: When the people heard these stern words, they went into mourning and stopped wearing their jewelry and fine clothes.
NLT.5: For the LORD had told Moses to tell them, “You are a stubborn and rebellious people. If I were to travel with you for even a moment, I would destroy you. Remove your jewelry and fine clothes while I decide what to do with you.”
NLT.6: So from the time they left Mount Sinai, the Israelites wore no more jewelry or fine clothes.
NLT.7: It was Moses’ practice to take the Tent of Meeting and set it up some distance from the camp. Everyone who wanted to make a request of the LORD would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.
NLT.8: Whenever Moses went out to the Tent of Meeting, all the people would get up and stand in the entrances of their own tents. They would all watch Moses until he disappeared inside.
NLT.9: As he went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and hover at its entrance while the LORD spoke with Moses.
NLT.10: When the people saw the cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, they would stand and bow down in front of their own tents.
NLT.11: Inside the Tent of Meeting, the LORD would speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend. Afterward Moses would return to the camp, but the young man who assisted him, Joshua son of Nun, would remain behind in the Tent of Meeting.
NLT.12: One day Moses said to the LORD, “You have been telling me, ‘Take these people up to the Promised Land.’ But you haven’t told me whom you will send with me. You have told me, ‘I know you by name, and I look favorably on you.’
NLT.13: If it is true that you look favorably on me, let me know your ways so I may understand you more fully and continue to enjoy your favor. And remember that this nation is your very own people.”
NLT.14: The LORD replied, “I will personally go with you, Moses, and I will give you rest — everything will be fine for you.”
NLT.15: Then Moses said, “If you don’t personally go with us, don’t make us leave this place.
NLT.16: How will anyone know that you look favorably on me — on me and on your people — if you don’t go with us? For your presence among us sets your people and me apart from all other people on the earth.”
NLT.17: The LORD replied to Moses, “I will indeed do what you have asked, for I look favorably on you, and I know you by name.”
NLT.18: Moses responded, “Then show me your glorious presence.”
NLT.19: The LORD replied, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and I will call out my name, Yahweh, before you. For I will show mercy to anyone I choose, and I will show compassion to anyone I choose.
NLT.20: But you may not look directly at my face, for no one may see me and live.”
NLT.21: The LORD continued, “Look, stand near me on this rock.
NLT.22: As my glorious presence passes by, I will hide you in the crevice of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
NLT.23: Then I will remove my hand and let you see me from behind. But my face will not be seen.”

WEB.2: I will send an angel before you; and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, and the Hittite, and the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite:
WEB.3: to a land flowing with milk and honey: for I will not go up among you, for you are a stiff-necked people, lest I consume you on the way.”
WEB.4: When the people heard this evil news, they mourned: and no one put on his jewelry.
WEB.5: Yahweh said to Moses, “Tell the children of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I were to go up into the middle of you for one moment, I would consume you. Therefore now take off your jewelry from you, that I may know what to do to you.’”
WEB.6: The children of Israel stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb onward.
WEB.7: Now Moses used to take the tent and to pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp, and he called it “The Tent of Meeting.” Everyone who sought Yahweh went out to the Tent of Meeting, which was outside the camp.
WEB.8: When Moses went out to the Tent, that all the people rose up, and stood, everyone at their tent door, and watched Moses, until he had gone into the Tent.
WEB.9: When Moses entered into the Tent, the pillar of cloud descended, stood at the door of the Tent, and spoke with Moses.
WEB.10: All the people saw the pillar of cloud stand at the door of the Tent, and all the people rose up and worshiped, everyone at their tent door.
WEB.11: Yahweh spoke to Moses face to face, as a man speaks to his friend. He turned again into the camp, but his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
WEB.12: Moses said to Yahweh, “Behold, you tell me, ‘Bring up this people:’ and you haven’t let me know whom you will send with me. Yet you have said, ‘I know you by name, and you have also found favor in my sight.’
WEB.13: Now therefore, if I have found favor in your sight, please show me now your way, that I may know you, so that I may find favor in your sight: and consider that this nation is your people.”
WEB.14: He said, “My presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
WEB.15: He said to him, “If your presence doesn’t go with me, don’t carry us up from here.
WEB.16: For how would people know that I have found favor in your sight, I and your people? Isn’t it that you go with us, so that we are separated, I and your people, from all the people who are on the surface of the earth?”
WEB.17: Yahweh said to Moses, “I will do this thing also that you have spoken; for you have found favor in my sight, and I know you by name.”
WEB.18: He said, “Please show me your glory.”
WEB.19: He said, “I will make all my goodness pass before you, and will proclaim Yahweh’s name before you. I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show mercy on whom I will show mercy.”
WEB.20: He said, “You cannot see my face, for man may not see me and live.”
WEB.21: Yahweh also said, “Behold, there is a place by me, and you shall stand on the rock.
WEB.22: It will happen, while my glory passes by, that I will put you in a cleft of the rock, and will cover you with my hand until I have passed by;
WEB.23: then I will take away my hand, and you will see my back; but my face shall not be seen.”

AMP.1: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying, "Depart, go up from here, you and the people whom you have brought from the land of Egypt, to the land which I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (Israel), saying, 'To your descendants I will give it.'
AMP.2: I will send an Angel before you and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite.
AMP.3: Go up to a land [of abundance] flowing with milk and honey; for I will not go up in your midst, because you are a stiff-necked (stubborn, rebellious) people, and I might destroy you on the way."
AMP.4: When the people heard this sad word, they mourned, and none of them put on his ornaments.
AMP.5: For the LORD had said to Moses, "Say to the sons of Israel, 'You are a stiff-necked (stubborn, rebellious) people! If I should come among you for one moment, I would destroy you. Now therefore, [penitently] take off your ornaments, so that I may know what to do with you.'"
AMP.6: So the Israelites left off all their ornaments [in repentance], from Mount Horeb (Sinai) onward.
AMP.7: Now Moses used to take his own tent and pitch it outside the camp, far away from the camp, and he called it the tent of meeting [of God with His own people]. And everyone who sought the LORD would go out to the [temporary] tent of meeting which was outside the camp.
AMP.8: Whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people would rise and stand, each at his tent door, and look at Moses until he entered the tent.
AMP.9: Whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the doorway of the tent; and the LORD would speak with Moses.
AMP.10: When all the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the tent door, all the people would rise and worship, each at his tent door.
AMP.11: And so the LORD used to speak to Moses face to face, just as a man speaks to his friend. When Moses returned to the camp, his attendant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, would not depart from the tent.
AMP.12: Moses said to the LORD, "See, You say to me, 'Bring up this people,' but You have not let me know whom You will send with me. Yet You have said, 'I know you by name, and you have also found favor in My sight.'
AMP.13: Now therefore, I pray you, if I have found favor in Your sight, let me know Your ways so that I may know You [becoming more deeply and intimately acquainted with You, recognizing and understanding Your ways more clearly] and that I may find grace and favor in Your sight. And consider also, that this nation is Your people."
AMP.14: And the LORD said, "My presence shall go with you, and I will give you rest [by bringing you and the people into the promised land]."
AMP.15: And Moses said to Him, "If Your presence does not go [with me], do not lead us up from here.
AMP.16: For how then can it be known that Your people and I have found favor in Your sight? Is it not by Your going with us, so that we are distinguished, Your people and I, from all the [other] people on the face of the earth?"
AMP.17: The LORD said to Moses, "I will also do this thing that you have asked; for you have found favor (lovingkindness, mercy) in My sight and I have known you [personally] by name."
AMP.18: Then Moses said, "Please, show me Your glory!"
AMP.19: And God said, "I will make all My goodness pass before you, and I will proclaim the Name of the LORD before you; for I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and will show compassion (lovingkindness) on whom I will show compassion."
AMP.20: But He said, "You cannot see My face, for no man shall see Me and live!"
AMP.21: Then the LORD said, "Behold, there is a place beside Me, and you shall stand there on the rock;
AMP.22: and while My glory is passing by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and protectively cover you with My hand until I have passed by.
AMP.23: Then I will take away My hand and you shall see My back; but My face shall not be seen."

MSG.1: God said to Moses: "Now go. Get on your way from here, you and the people you brought up from the land of Egypt. Head for the land which I promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying 'I will give it to your descendants.'
MSG.2: I will send an angel ahead of you and I'll drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.
MSG.3: It's a land flowing with milk and honey. But I won't be with you in person—you're such a stubborn, hard-headed people!—lest I destroy you on the journey."
MSG.4: When the people heard this harsh verdict, they were plunged into gloom and wore long faces. No one put on jewelry.
MSG.5: God said to Moses, "Tell the Israelites, 'You're one hard-headed people. I couldn't stand being with you for even a moment—I'd destroy you. So take off all your jewelry until I figure out what to do with you.' "
MSG.6: So the Israelites stripped themselves of their jewelry from Mount Horeb on.
MSG.7: Moses used to take the Tent and set it up outside the camp, some distance away. He called it the Tent of Meeting. Anyone who sought God would go to the Tent of Meeting outside the camp.
MSG.8: It went like this: When Moses would go to the Tent, all the people would stand at attention; each man would take his position at the entrance to his tent with his eyes on Moses until he entered the Tent;
MSG.9: whenever Moses entered the Tent, the Pillar of Cloud descended to the entrance to the Tent and God spoke with Moses.
MSG.10: All the people would see the Pillar of Cloud at the entrance to the Tent, stand at attention, and then bow down in worship, each man at the entrance to his tent.
MSG.11: And God spoke with Moses face-to-face, as neighbors speak to one another. When he would return to the camp, his attendant, the young man Joshua, stayed—he didn't leave the Tent.
MSG.12: Moses said to God, "Look, you tell me, 'Lead this people,' but you don't let me know whom you're going to send with me. You tell me, 'I know you well and you are special to me.'
MSG.13: If I am so special to you, let me in on your plans. That way, I will continue being special to you. Don't forget, this is your people, your responsibility."
MSG.14: God said, "My presence will go with you. I'll see the journey to the end."
MSG.15: Moses said, "If your presence doesn't take the lead here, call this trip off right now.

MSG.17: God said to Moses: "All right. Just as you say; this also I will do, for I know you well and you are special to me. I know you by name."
MSG.18: Moses said, "Please. Let me see your Glory."

NIV.1: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Leave this place, you and the people you brought up out of Egypt, and go up to the land I promised on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, saying, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’
NIV.2: I will send an angel before you and drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
NIV.3: Go up to the land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go with you, because you are a stiff-necked people and I might destroy you on the way.”
NIV.4: When the people heard these distressing words, they began to mourn and no one put on any ornaments.
NIV.5: For the Lord had said to Moses, “Tell the Israelites, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. If I were to go with you even for a moment, I might destroy you. Now take off your ornaments and I will decide what to do with you.’”
NIV.6: So the Israelites stripped off their ornaments at Mount Horeb.
NIV.7:
The Tent of Meeting
Now Moses used to take a tent and pitch it outside the camp some distance away, calling it the “tent of meeting.” Anyone inquiring of the Lord would go to the tent of meeting outside the camp.
NIV.8: And whenever Moses went out to the tent, all the people rose and stood at the entrances to their tents, watching Moses until he entered the tent.
NIV.9: As Moses went into the tent, the pillar of cloud would come down and stay at the entrance, while the Lord spoke with Moses.
NIV.10: Whenever the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they all stood and worshiped, each at the entrance to his tent.
NIV.11: The Lord would speak to Moses face to face, as a man speaks with his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young aide Joshua son of Nun did not leave the tent.
NIV.12:
Moses and the Glory of the Lord
Moses said to the Lord, “You have been telling me, ‘Lead these people,’ but you have not let me know whom you will send with me. You have said, ‘I know you by name and you have found favor with me.’
NIV.13: If you are pleased with me, teach me your ways so I may know you and continue to find favor with you. Remember that this nation is your people.”
NIV.14: The Lord replied, “My Presence will go with you, and I will give you rest.”
NIV.15: Then Moses said to him, “If your Presence does not go with us, do not send us up from here.
NIV.16: How will anyone know that you are pleased with me and with your people unless you go with us? What else will distinguish me and your people from all the other people on the face of the earth?”
NIV.17: And the Lord said to Moses, “I will do the very thing you have asked, because I am pleased with you and I know you by name.”
NIV.18: Then Moses said, “Now show me your glory.”
NIV.19: And the Lord said, “I will cause all my goodness to pass in front of you, and I will proclaim my name, the Lord, in your presence. I will have mercy on whom I will have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I will have compassion.
NIV.20: But,” he said, “you cannot see my face, for no one may see me and live.”
NIV.21: Then the Lord said, “There is a place near me where you may stand on a rock.
NIV.22: When my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft in the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
NIV.23: Then I will remove my hand and you will see my back; but my face must not be seen.”
